about.label: About
about.statement: I turn complex problems into products used by millions of people. I blend architecture, quality and leadership with something rare in engineering: a degree in Psychology.
paragraphs: At itti I'm Tech Lead and Engineering Manager for growth in the apps division: I take teams and products from concept to production. As AI Champion I also bring AI into the engineering teams' daily work, with agents and without trading off quality.

I'm obsessed with teams delivering what they promise. That's why every initiative starts from a PRD and an RFC, with tests as a safety net and standardized agent workflows, so the speed AI adds isn't paid for with technical debt.

That background lets me lead with a people-centered approach: technical interviews, mentoring and career development plans that help other developers grow, something I also did as a Full Stack teacher.

testimonials.label: Testimonials
testimonials.title: What people I've worked with say

bertalot.name: Leandro Bertalot
bertalot.role: Engineering leadership · Fintech & platforms · Ex Mercado Libre, Tiendanube and Ualá
bertalot.quote: He's one of those people who raise the team's bar just by being there.
bertalot.text:
I was lucky to work with Nico and, no beating around the bush: he's one of those people who raise the team's bar just by being there.
Professionally, he delivers with a quality you can see in every detail. He understands the problem, proposes, executes and closes. He adopts AI tools with judgment —not because they're trendy— and that translates into more speed and better results without losing craft.
But what stands out most is the person: generous, clear, good-natured and the kind who has your back when you need to push. Working with him is easy and makes you want to keep going.
Any team that brings him on wins from day one. I recommend him without hesitation.

gonzalez.name: Deivid Steven Gonzalez
gonzalez.relation: Teammate on the Mobile Core team
gonzalez.quote: He knows how to guide without imposing and shares what he knows generously.
gonzalez.text:
I had the opportunity to work with Joel on the Mobile Core team and I can say without a doubt that he's one of those people who make the whole team better.
Technically he's solid and isn't afraid of hard things: on projects like uMarket and Tuiu he always went after the most complex challenges. We had to refactor a codebase in very bad shape, and with him it was easy to turn it around while meeting high quality and security standards (SonarQube, Checkmarx and unit tests).
But what sets him apart most is his natural leadership and willingness to help. He knows how to guide without imposing and shares what he knows generously. It was common to see him with the backend tech lead planning, supporting and testing new developments, or lending a hand to any role on the team that needed it.
Working with him is easy and motivating. Any team that has him will gain not just a great professional, but a great teammate. I fully recommend him.

martinez.name: Nacho Martínez
martinez.role: Mobile Tech Lead · Content Creator · Director of El Container
martinez.quote: He has that valuable mix of technical depth and big-picture vision.
martinez.text:
I had the pleasure of having Nicolás on my team, and he's one of those professionals who stand out for both their technical ability and their human quality.
Nicolás has a huge ability to communicate, empathize and connect with people. He builds trust naturally, knows how to listen and has a great capacity to become a reference for a team. His leadership isn't only about what he knows, but also about how he supports others, creates a good working environment and helps the whole team grow.
Technically, he has a very solid level of seniority, broad knowledge and a constant curiosity to keep learning. He always seeks to understand a bit more, anticipate challenges and find practical solutions. He has that valuable mix of technical depth and big-picture vision that lets him move comfortably across different projects and contexts.
I especially highlight how he handles complex or urgent situations. He knows how to stay calm, analyze problems with judgment and pass that calm on to the rest of the team, something I consider essential in any leadership position.
And, of course, there's his great attitude. Always smiling, open to talk, share knowledge and bring a constructive perspective. He's one of those people it's a pleasure to work with and from whom you always end up learning something.
I'm very grateful to have had the chance to work with Nicolás and have him on my team. He's a professional I recommend without hesitation, both for what he can bring technically and for his ability to lead, support and empower the people who work with him.

framework.name: godot-studio-skills
framework.lead: The chat doesn't make the game: it orchestrates it.
framework.description: A kit of skills, commands and subagents that turns Claude Code or Cursor into a small studio. The orchestrator interviews you, writes the PRD and RFCs, and hands plan, code, review and playtest to subagents with isolated roles. The result isn't a thousand-line World.gd: it's a small, playable, clear base that a human or another AI can continue.
principles: Spec-driven: PRD, RFCs and an approved file tree before a single line is written.
You choose the architecture you want to use, and the framework follows it end to end.
One RFC at a time: plan, build, review and playtest on every slice.
Done means verified: it parses headless, passes gdformat and gdlint, and the scene runs.

flow.label: One feature, from idea to close
flow.loop: If the playtest fails, the orchestrator classifies the report and sends it back to the developer, reviewer or playtester. A slice closes only when it passes.

caseStudy.name: Sacrifice
caseStudy.description: I used the framework to port Shiny Entertainment's 2000 strategy classic to Godot 4 and export it to the web. The migration moved feature by feature with SDD: spec, tech-lead plan, implementation, review and automated playtest before closing each slice.
caseStudy.note: Non-commercial fan project. Original assets belong to their owners.
